guide.summary: Production agent connecting customers' Gusto (app review, wait about 1-2 months from demo keys to production keys).
guide.verdict: No easy case: every production integration needs Gusto's pre-approval, security review and QA, which Gusto usually estimates at 1-2 months after demo keys.

composio.note: Gusto is listed under bring-your-own OAuth apps; create the auth config with your own client ID and secret.

need_own_app.answer: Yes. Composio has no managed Gusto app, so you must register your own app in Gusto's Developer Portal and give Composio its client ID and secret.
reasons: Composio lists Gusto only under bring-your-own OAuth apps
Managed apps would show 'Composio wants to access your account' on the consent screen
Managed apps share quota across all Composio users

scenarios.label: Production agent connecting customers' Gusto
scenarios.when_this_applies: Any app that lets outside Gusto customers connect their company through OAuth in production.

hands_on.basis: estimate from step count (questionnaire, security documents, demo testing), not measured

waiting.estimate: About 1-2 months from demo keys to production keys
waiting.basis: c17 (Gusto's estimate; depends on integration type; pre-approval wait itself not stated)

scenarios.approval: Production Pre-Approval by the Partnerships team, then a Security Review by the GRC team, then a QA review before production keys are issued.
extras: Only primary or full access admins can authorize

modifiers.note: Only primary or full access admins can authorize the app

prerequisites.title: Gusto Developer Account
prerequisites.detail: Sign up, accept the terms and create an application to get API keys.

prerequisites.title: Security documentation
prerequisites.detail: Prepare audits such as SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001 with SOA or PCI DSS, plus penetration test reports. Without a formal audit, describe your security controls.

prerequisites.title: Security and incident contacts
prerequisites.detail: Provide a security contact and an incident response contact, each with name, title and email.

prerequisites.title: Own redirect URI
prerequisites.detail: Gusto generates client ID and secret when you supply a redirect URI. Wildcards and fragments are not allowed.

steps.title: Sign up for a Gusto Developer Account
steps.detail: Accept the terms and create an application to get demo keys.
steps.done_when: Demo API keys appear in the Developer Portal.

steps.title: Draft Production Pre-Approval answers
steps.detail: Draft the use case, scope justification and security answers; the questionnaire also feeds the Security Review.
steps.done_when: Draft answers are ready for review.

steps.title: Submit Production Pre-Approval
steps.detail: Attach audit reports, pen test reports and contacts, then submit.

steps.title: Wait for pre-approval and Security Review
steps.detail: Partnerships reviews first, then GRC. Reply quickly to any information request, as the review is on hold until you do.
steps.done_when: Gusto emails approval and next steps.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the auth config with your own client ID and secret via Composio's API; copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard.

steps.title: Test all scopes in demo
steps.detail: Test the integration and assigned scopes against api.gusto-demo.com.
steps.done_when: Integration works in demo and is ready for QA.

steps.title: Wait for QA and production keys
steps.detail: Gusto runs QA, then issues production credentials in the Developer Portal.
steps.done_when: Production credentials are in the Developer Portal.

traps.title: Since v2023-05-01, a user authorizing multiple companies must complete
traps.detail: Since v2023-05-01, a user authorizing multiple companies must complete the OAuth2 flow for each company individually.

traps.title: Production redirect changes need Gusto
traps.detail: Demo redirect URIs can be edited in the portal, but changing the production redirect requires emailing Gusto.

traps.title: Scopes are assigned, not chosen
traps.detail: Calls outside assigned scopes are rejected in production, and extra scopes can only be requested after production release.

traps.title: One OAuth flow per company
traps.detail: Since v2023-05-01, each access token covers one company, so multi-company admins must authorize each separately.

traps.title: No production test accounts
traps.detail: All testing, before and after launch, must happen in the demo environment.

blockers.what_it_means: Gusto asked for more information and is waiting for your answer.
blockers.what_to_do: Watch your email and respond promptly.
blockers.agent_can_help: Draft responses and assemble the documents.

blockers.what_it_means: You exceeded 200 requests in a 60-second rolling window for a grant.
blockers.what_to_do: Throttle and retry after the window closes.
blockers.agent_can_help: Add rate limiting and backoff to the client.

evidence.answer: The Composio callback URL used in the proxy example is https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Composio registers and maintains OAuth apps for popular toolkits such as GitHub, Gmail, and Slack.
evidence.answer: Composio registers and maintains OAuth apps for popular toolkits (the page names GitHub, Gmail, and Slack as examples). This is a general statement; the page does not say whether Gusto has a managed app.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: You do not need to register your own OAuth app.
evidence.answer: For toolkits with a Composio managed app, the developer does not need to register their own OAuth app.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: You provide your own OAuth app, API key, bearer token, or other credentials and tell Composio to use them for a toolkit.
evidence.answer: With a custom auth config, the developer supplies their own OAuth app, API key, bearer token, or other credentials and tells Composio to use them for a toolkit.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Composio's default scopes may not include everything you need (e.g., write access to a specific Google API).
evidence.answer: Composio's managed apps request sensible default scopes for each toolkit. The page says default scopes may not cover every need, for example write access to a specific Google API.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Managed apps share quota across all Composio users.
evidence.answer: Managed apps are shared across all Composio users, so their quota is shared. A custom app gets a dedicated quota.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval; your own app can use shorter polling intervals where supported.
evidence.answer: Managed auth enforces a minimum polling interval of 15 minutes for polling triggers. A developer's own app can use shorter polling intervals where supported.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Users will see "Composio wants to access your account" during OAuth.
evidence.answer: With a managed app, users see OAuth consent screens that say Composio wants to access their account, not the developer's app name. The page says production users should see the app name, which is the most common reason to switch to a custom app.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: In production, users should see your app name, not "Composio." This is the most common reason to switch.
evidence.answer: In production, users should see the developer's app name rather than Composio on the consent screen, which is the most common reason to switch to a custom app.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: The id and secret will be generated when you supply a redirect_uri to Gusto.
evidence.answer: Gusto generates the client ID and secret when the developer supplies a redirect_uri to Gusto. The page does not describe any app review, verification, marketplace listing, or partner acceptance step.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: Only primary admins or full access admins on the Gusto account can enable and authenticate a new application’s access (the “user” in the outline below).
evidence.answer: Only primary admins or full access admins on the Gusto account can enable and authenticate a new application's access.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: During the authorization step, Gusto will automatically prompt the user to select which company they would like to provide access to.
evidence.answer: During authorization, Gusto prompts the admin to select which company to give the application access to.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: Note: As of version v2023-05-01 , if the user wishes to authorize multiple companies, they must go through the OAuth2 flow for each company individually
evidence.answer: As of v2023-05-01, an administrator who wants to authorize multiple companies must go through the OAuth2 flow separately for each company.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: Our May 2023 release, v2023-05-01 , introduced strict access , which restricts an access token to only one company, meaning a multi-company administrator must go through OAuth individually for each company they wish to authorize.
evidence.answer: Since v2023-05-01 (strict access), each access token is restricted to one company, so a multi-company administrator must authorize each company through OAuth individually.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: OAuth2 does not support wildcard URIs or URIs with fragments (e.g #).
evidence.answer: OAuth2 redirect URIs cannot use wildcards or include URI fragments.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: redirect_uri - the percent-encoded url you submitted when signing up for the Gusto API.
evidence.answer: The redirect_uri parameter in the authorization link must be the percent-encoded URL the developer submitted when signing up for the Gusto API.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: redirect_uri - the redirect URI you set up via the Developer Portal
evidence.answer: The redirect_uri sent in the token exchange must be the redirect URI the developer set up via the Developer Portal.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Your demo application redirect URI(s) can be changed via the Applications tab of your Developer Portal account.
evidence.answer: Demo application redirect URIs can be changed in the Applications tab of the developer's Developer Portal account.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: To change the redirect for your Production Application, please reach out to [email protected]
evidence.answer: To change the redirect for a Production Application, the developer must contact Gusto by email rather than change it in the portal.
